meaning: Transmural pressure of this vessel element is defined as the internal pressure minus the external pressure at its `ext` port, so all downstream area/compliance behaviour is driven by that difference rather than by absolute internal pressure. Every external-pressure input (Pext, Pabdo, postural, jugular compression) enters the collapsible-vessel mechanics only through this line.

could_move.what: Area, and hence flow resistance and volume, since A is computed from V but V responds to Ptm through the constitutive law in this element
Mass split between in/out/ext ports, because ext.q is tied to the same external port whose pressure sets Ptm
All external-pressure sweep decks, whose whole effect is mediated by ext.p
Abdominal pressure decks, same mediation path
Patient-fit comparisons for jugular compression, if Ptm sign or reference changes

expectation: Unknown in size. Directionally, any change to this definition (sign, added reference term, or dropping ext.p) shifts collapse onset and thus the amplitude of the response to external-pressure manoeuvres. I cannot tell from this context whether fitted parameters absorb it.

check.why: Re-runs the existing fit verification for m1 without a full re-fit, so a changed Ptm definition shows up as a shift in fitted-case residuals before any sweep or replot is trusted.
